text:
Will Cuylle is the Rangers' heavy winger who keeps getting good looks and not enough goals. He has four on 6.27 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and the Rangers have scored 5.1 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That's our textbook definition of due: the process is fine, the finish is late. One goal in his last ten games is the part fans notice; 2.7 expected goals in that stretch is the part that should calm them.

The Rangers tried him at centre this month, and the reviews from Newsday and others were kind, but Yahoo Sports reported by Nov. 9 that the experiment was already ending. That fits who he is. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him as a finisher of other people's passes across the slot and a dump-and-chase forward who rarely carries the puck in. Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season liked his defence most: opponents got noticeably fewer chances with him out there (94th percentile). Our projection has him around 20 goals. Watch the third line he's anchoring with Laba and Bjorkstrand: if the bounces turn, it's his line that benefits first.
